bsb.text: A wise son heeds his father’s discipline, but a mocker does not listen to rebuke.

explanation.text:
shall eat--that is, obtain (Pro 12:14).

transgressors--as in Pro 2:22.

violence--or, "mischief" to themselves.

bsb.text: From the fruit of his lips a man enjoys good things, but the desire of the faithless is violence.

explanation.text:
He . . . mouth . . . life--because evil speeches may provoke violence from others.

he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction--On last clause, compare Pro 10:14.

bsb.text: He who guards his mouth protects his life, but the one who opens his lips invites his own ruin.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 12:11, Pro 12:27).

bsb.text: The slacker craves yet has nothing, but the soul of the diligent is fully satisfied.

explanation.text: loathsome . . . shame--better, causeth shame and reproach (compare Pro 19:26), by slander, etc., which the righteous hates.

bsb.text: The righteous hate falsehood, but the wicked bring shame and disgrace.

explanation.text: A sentiment of frequent recurrence, that piety benefits and sin injures.

bsb.text: Righteousness guards the man of integrity, but wickedness undermines the sinner.

explanation.text: In opposite ways men act hypocritically for gain of honor or wealth.

bsb.text: One pretends to be rich, but has nothing; another pretends to be poor, yet has great wealth.

explanation.text: Riches save some from punishment, while others suffer because they will not heed the rebuke of sloth, which makes and keeps them poor.

bsb.text: Riches may ransom a man’s life, but a poor man hears no threat.

explanation.text:
light . . . lamp--prosperity; the first, the greater, and it

rejoiceth--burns brightly, or continues, while the other, at best small, soon fails.

bsb.text: The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is extinguished.

explanation.text: The obstinacy which attends self-conceit, produces contention, which the well-advised, thus evincing modesty, avoid.

bsb.text: Arrogance leads only to strife, but wisdom is with the well-advised.

explanation.text:
by vanity--or, "nothingness," that is, which is vain or useless to the public (as card playing or similar vices).

gathereth . . . labour--(Compare Margin), little by little, laboriously.

bsb.text: Dishonest wealth will dwindle, but what is earned through hard work will be multiplied.

explanation.text:
desire cometh--is realized.

a tree of life--or, "cause of happiness."

bsb.text: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life.

explanation.text: the word--that is, of advice, or, instruction (compare Pro 10:27; Pro 11:31).

bsb.text: He who despises instruction will pay the penalty, but the one who respects a command will be rewarded.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 10:11).

fountain--or, "source of life."

to depart--(compare Pro 1:2-4), or, "for departing," etc., and so gives life.

bsb.text: The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning one from the snares of death.

explanation.text:
Right perception and action secure good will, while evil ways are difficult as a stony road. The wicked left of God find punishment of sin in sinning.

hard--or, "harsh" (compare Hebrew: Deu 21:4; Jer 5:15).

bsb.text: Good understanding wins favor, but the way of the faithless is difficult.

explanation.text:
dealeth--acts with foresight.

a fool . . . folly--for want of caution.

bsb.text: Every prudent man acts with knowledge, but a fool displays his folly.

explanation.text:
A wicked--or, "unfaithful"

messenger falleth into mischief--or, "by mischief," or "evil," and so his errand fails. Contrasted is the character of the faithful, whose faithfulness benefits others.

bsb.text: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 10:17; Pro 12:1).

bsb.text: Poverty and shame come to him who ignores discipline, but whoever heeds correction is honored.

explanation.text: Self-denial, which fools will not endure, is essential to success.

bsb.text: Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but turning from evil is detestable to fools.

explanation.text: The benefits of good and evil of bad society are contrasted.

bsb.text: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 11:31).

good . . . repaid--or, "He (God) will repay good."

bsb.text: Disaster pursues sinners, but prosperity is the reward of the righteous.

explanation.text: wealth . . . just--While good men's estates remain in their families, God so orders that the gains of sinners enure to the just (compare Pro 28:8; Psa 37:18, Psa 37:22, Psa 37:26, etc.).

bsb.text: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the sinner’s wealth is passed to the righteous.

explanation.text: The laboring poor prosper more than those who injudiciously or wickedly strive, by fraud and violence, to supersede the necessity of lawful labor.

bsb.text: Abundant food is in the fallow ground of the poor, but without justice it is swept away.

explanation.text:
spareth--or, "withholds."

rod--of correction.

hateth--or, acts as if he hated him (compare Pro 3:12; Pro 8:36).

chasteneth . . . betimes--or, "diligently seeks for him all useful discipline."

bsb.text: He who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him diligently.

explanation.text:
The comparative temporal prosperity of the righteous and wicked, rather than contentment and discontent, is noted.

Next: Proverbs Chapter 14

bsb.text: A righteous man eats to his heart’s content, but the stomach of the wicked is empty.
